summary.text: 工 is a whole-graph pictograph interpreted as a tool. Its exact referent is disputed; early examples also use the graph for names, titles, and occupations, while its current senses include work and labor. The evidence does not establish one sequence linking these uses.

formation.text: Pictographic: early forms are described as tool-like, but proposals differ between a bladed tool (possibly also used as a carpenter’s square), a square, and a building tool. These are readings of the whole graph, not analyses of separate components. A transmitted historical account instead explains 工 as 巧飾 and interprets the form as a person with measuring tools; this is a different explanation, not independent confirmation of the pictured object.

components.text: 工 is treated as one complete pictorial graph, interpreted as a tool. The precise object remains disputed, and no separate internal components are identified.

history.text: Early oracle-bone and bronze forms are described as tool-like. Some early bronze forms have a thicker lower stroke, but the evidence does not support tracing a particular sequence of graphic changes.
A transmitted historical account records 𢒄, which contains 彡, as an ancient form of 工. Its relationship to 工—whether ancestor, variant, or another kind of connection—is unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The proposed object is disputed, and its name and pronunciation are not established.工’s reconstructed readings do not identify the object. The cited early artifacts are not dated in the account, so they do not establish the earliest attestation of each use.

It is unclear whether early official or status uses relate to craft and work, or whether these meanings form a chronological chain. 工 is also reported as a whole-graph loan for 貢 in oracle-bone contexts, but the sound comparison and dates are not established here.

senses.text: The graph is interpreted as picturing a tool, but the precise object is disputed. The cited account does not date the relevant artifacts, so this is not a securely dated earliest word meaning.
Reported oracle-bone examples use 工 as a state or place name. This use is not connected to the proposed tool meaning.

senses.gloss: official title, status, or occupation term
senses.period: oracle-bone and bronze examples; dating unresolved
senses.text: Reported examples use 工 for status or occupation and in official titles. Their relationship to craft and work uses is unresolved.

senses.period: early examples and received Zhouli tradition; dating unresolved
senses.text: Reported examples use 工 for craft workers, including 百工. The received Zhouli tradition also uses it for skilled makers, but these attestations do not date the sense’s beginning or show how it relates to the tool interpretation.
工 currently means work or labor. The evidence does not give a dated sequence showing how these senses developed from the proposed tool or craft-worker senses.

senses.gloss: achievement, written with 工 for 功
senses.period: bronze inscriptions and Warring States bamboo slip; artifact dates unresolved here
senses.text: In cited contexts, 工 is read as 功, ‘achievement’. This is graphic interchange or borrowing in those contexts, not proof that 工’s work sense developed into achievement.

senses.gloss: tribute or offering, written with 工 for 貢
senses.text: In reported oracle-bone contexts, 工 writes 貢. This proposed whole-graph loan means the sign was reused for another word because the words were said to sound alike or similarly, not because the tool meaning changed into ‘tribute’. The early sound match is not independently established by the cited account.

limitations.text: The cited account does not date the artifact examples, so the senses listed here cannot be arranged into a secure chronology. Glosses alone do not demonstrate semantic development.

The proposed tool referent, the relationship between early official or status uses and craft or work uses, and the sound basis of the 貢 loan remain unresolved. Close reconstructed readings for 工, 功, and 攻 do not establish a shared semantic history.

overview.text: 工 is a whole-graph picture interpreted as a tool, though the exact object is disputed. Today it means work or labor; early uses also include occupations, but the evidence does not link these meanings in a clear sequence.

components.text: Read 工 as one complete picture, proposed to show a tool. The exact object is uncertain; no separate internal components are identified.
